reason: Reject the steering action. Photographic surfaces and face stability are useful, but the hands leave the wheel and mime a control that does not exist. It cannot supply the human story payoff.
reviewer: Codex decoded-frame and native keyframe inspection

criteria.criterion: Photographic person, boat fittings and moving water
criteria.observation: Stable face, clothing and deck/water textures in all 49 decoded frames and native-resolution keyframes.

criteria.criterion: A physically connected, purposeful steering adjustment
criteria.observation: The right hand leaves the actual wheel then both fists move around an invisible control in front of the torso; no coherent grip/rotation response.

criteria.criterion: The sailor commits her attention to the horizon
criteria.observation: Gaze stays substantially toward the camera with a brief side glance, rather than completing the planned look toward open water.

revisionInstructions: Keep the source-supported right hand on the wheel and left hand on the rail throughout. Animate an intentional head turn toward open water and body balance against the swell; do not request a second grip or ungrounded hand choreography. Preserve this rejected take and use a new artifact identity.
limitations: Decoded visual inspection, not a completed soundtrack/whole-film viewer review.
